title: Planner Unknowns section: four quadrants, mandatory per epic plan
subject: planner-unknowns-section
ratio: Every epic plan carries a populated Unknowns section in four quadrants - known-knowns, known-unknowns, unknown-knowns, unknown-unknowns - before any task publishes. Every known-unknown is classified BLOCKING or NON-BLOCKING, and every BLOCKING known-unknown is closed before the DAG is published, by exactly one of two paths: converting it into a spike task that every DAG node needing the answer lists in depends_on, so the cascade gate mechanically prevents early claims, or posing it as a numbered question to the human and recording the answer in the plan. A DAG with an unresolved BLOCKING known-unknown must not be published. Reach, stated exactly: this duty lives ONLY in the orchestration-planner's agent-definition file (.claude/agents/orchestration-planner.md, protocol step 6) and binds planner protocol - whoever drafts and publishes the epic plan - not all agents. The Unknowns sections and the TEMPLATE block in .harness/plan.md are the artifact the duty produces, not a second home of it. It was never promoted into ORCHESTRATION.md, and this record does not widen it: its reach is deliberately narrower than that of the verifier-rotation rule born of the same audit (F6, already codified as PR-004), which did reach ORCHESTRATION.md and the registry. Reach and authority tier are different axes and this record claims only the first: the tier states how well the norm is evidenced, never how far it binds.
dicta: Origin: audit_gen3.md section 5.5 (the U1 proposal) and section 4 row 13. NUMBERING CAUTION: the audit DOCUMENT calls this proposal P-014, while the accepted-mutation ledger entry in state.json evolution.accepted_mutations carries id P-015 - the two numberings are offset by one across this audit run, so P-015 is the citable token and section 5.5 is the readable text. U1 was pre-approved by the operator and applied at T-037, verdicted done by harness-verifier (events.jsonl ts 2026-07-05T03:13:57Z), an identity distinct from the producer substrate-worker-2. REACH, NOT TIER: the duty exists in exactly one operative place, the orchestration-planner agent definition, protocol step 6; ORCHESTRATION.md contains no Unknowns rule and never did - the audit's own pre-mutation grep for the word unknown across the planner file and plan.md returned zero, and P-015's target list names the agent definition and plan.md, not the topology contract. This is the single-homed row of the wave: unlike the blindspot interview, U1 has no downstream feed in AGENTS.md or any other agent file. It is deliberately narrower than PR-004, the verifier-rotation rule born of the same audit, which did reach ORCHESTRATION.md; PR-004 is named by prose reference and is not re-minted. CD6 HONESTY: P-015 is a code-level agent-definition mutation whose recorded gate reads code-level with U1 pre-approved by operator, not an NLAH mutation through the section 5A human gate, so under a strict reading of PRECEDENT.md section 3 this record would fall to tier 3 on T-037; the frozen ledger row chose tier 2 and the ledger's OPEN-QUESTION 5 names that fallback. The pre-approval is tier-1-shaped evidence in kind but is recorded in no human_gates entry and carries no isolating event token, so tier 1 is not claimed. LINE-ANCHOR HYGIENE: the gen-3 audit sourced U1 from a state.json LINE NUMBER that no longer points at that content, so this record anchors to the agent definition by a live line range and to the mutation by ledger key P-015, never to a state.json line. CITATION-RANGE NOTE: the frozen ledger row names the primary home as lines 36-38; protocol step 6 in fact spans lines 36-45, and the operative half - the BLOCKING classification, the two closure paths and the MUST NOT be published sentence - lives at 39-45, so this record cites the full range.
